title: Feitan vs Zazan: The Phantom Troupe Sadist Turns a Chimera Ant Queen to Ash

cuts.voiceover_text: In the wasteland of Meteor City, a web-covered nest belches green smoke into the sky. The Chimera Ant Zazan has crowned herself queen here, and the natives of this scrapyard city, the Phantom Troupe, have come to end her.

Deep in the nest, the hooded figure of Feitan walks past a corridor of dead ants and mutters that he needs to stop toying with his prey. The shot cuts to Zazan smirking down from her web, and Feitan quietly draws his blade.

The fight opens for real. Feitan blurs through the shadows while Zazan hurls her scorpion tail, shattering stone pillars around him. Watching from cover, the Troupe murmur that these two are on a completely different level.
Feitan slips in and slashes her face. Blood runs down Zazan's cheek from her eye, but instead of falling she throws her head back and screams. Her skin is tougher than he thought.

Feitan focuses every drop of his aura into one point to punch through her hide, but the instant he commits to Ko the rest of him is defenseless. Zazan swings a crude burst of aura that rips him open and sends him skidding back, shirtless and bleeding, as she roars that her body is indestructible.

Then she lands the strike that changes the fight. A grey burst erupts across Feitan's side and his left arm is gone. Down the corridor, the Troupe start backing away, warning each other that when Feitan snaps, his rage-triggered ability will obliterate everything around him.

Feitan's aura flares sickly green as he pulls a spiked robe over himself. When he lifts his head, he is wearing the burgundy-and-white armor of Pain Packer. High above Zazan a tiny second sun ignites in the air. She looks up in horror as its searing light swallows her whole, burning her monstrous body down to a silhouette of ash.

The heat fades. Feitan stands alone over the charred outline of what used to be the queen, a small cold smile on his face as he tells her that if she had only dealt him more damage, she might have had a good will. She had only herself to blame.
